lastCompletedStory.title: Stamp updatedAt on every issue-mutation writer

nextStoryContext: US-002 is done: every issue-mutation writer now overrides updatedAt to the injected clock() value on the mutated entry(ies), never touching createdAt. specifyIssueOnMain/abandonIssueOnMain/closeIssueOnMain/demoteIssueOnMain (all in src/commands/issue-specify.ts) destructure the clock already present on their (required) options and stamp it onto the mutated spread; mergeIssueOnMain stamps both the abandoned source (buildMergeFiles) and, when foldBlockedBy folds deps, the mutated target (withMergedBlockedBy). triage.ts's computeRankDiff now takes an optional `clock: ClockFn | undefined` threaded from RunTriageOptions.clock (still optional, still unforced) -- when present it stamps updatedAt on every rank-changed entry; when absent the entry's prior updatedAt is left untouched (no inline fallback). dispatchTriage (index.ts) is the sole production caller and now passes `clock: () => new Date().toISOString()` explicitly, since triage.ts itself must contain literally zero `new Date()`/`Date.now()` occurrences (this story's own AC#3 file-assert oracle greps for that pattern across issue-specify.ts + triage.ts with zero tolerance, including inside comments). Confirmed via grep that only these two files ever write an IssueEntry to disk (issueFilePath + `{ ...entry`/`{ ...issue`/`{ ...source`/`{ ...target` spreads) -- no other mutation path exists anywhere in src/. One incidental fix: specifyIssueOnMain's mutated-entry spread grew by one line and tripped Biome's noExcessiveLinesPerFunction (ceiling 80); fixed by collapsing its first guard to the one-line `if (!guard.ok) return guard;` style already used by its sibling functions in the same file (no biome.json override needed). Full quality spine (typecheck, bun test, bun run check:all) is green. Nothing else in the PRD is queued beyond US-002 as of this handoff -- check prd.json for the next story before assuming completion.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure in-repo TypeScript: threading an already-injected ClockFn through existing writer functions and one CLI dispatch call site. No new external library surface introduced or exercised.
